docs.title: Home
docs.text:
docker run -d --name arcanum -p 3100:3100 \
  -e GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  -v arcanum-data:/data \
  ghcr.io/rafaeldourado9/arcanum:latest

  • Light and fast

    A single Go binary built on whatsmeow. Tens of megabytes of RAM per session, starts in milliseconds, runs on a Raspberry Pi.

  • Anti-ban built in

    Typing indicator sized to the message, human-like random delay, per-minute limit and one message at a time per chat. On by default for every send.

  • Many numbers, one API

    Create as many sessions as you need. Each one has its own webhook, settings and rate limit. Sessions survive restarts.

  • Webhooks you can trust

    HMAC-SHA256 signature on every delivery, Meta Cloud API compatible format or a simple flat format, and a fromMe flag so your bot knows when a human took over.

  • Secure by default

    API key on every route, input validation, SSRF protection on webhooks, no personal data in logs, non-root container, vulnerability scans in CI.

  • Open source, MIT

    Read every line, fork it, run it anywhere. No license keys, no phone-home.

docs.title: WhatsApp API you host yourself
docs.text:
Arcanum is an open-source WhatsApp gateway written in Go. One small binary connects your WhatsApp numbers and gives you a REST API, signed webhooks and an anti-ban layer that behaves like a person typing. No browser, no Node, no vendor lock-in.

Get started in 5 minutes GitHub

docs.title: How it fits
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Your app] -- REST + API key --> B[Arcanum]
    B -- WhatsApp Web protocol --> C[(WhatsApp)]
    C -- incoming messages --> B
    B -- signed webhook --> A

Your application calls Arcanum to send messages. Arcanum keeps the WhatsApp sessions connected and posts every incoming message to your webhook.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Getting started: run it, scan the QR code, send your first message.
  • Webhooks: receive messages and verify the signature.
  • Deployment: put it in production behind HTTPS.

Not an official API

Arcanum talks to WhatsApp through the same protocol as WhatsApp Web. It is not affiliated with WhatsApp or Meta. Automated messaging can get numbers banned: respect WhatsApp's terms, message only people who expect to hear from you, and keep the anti-ban layer on.

docs.title: Anti-ban
docs.text: WhatsApp watches for accounts that behave like machines: instant replies, bursts of identical messages, no typing. Arcanum makes every text send look like a person wrote it.

docs.title: What happens on each text
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Your app
    participant A as Arcanum
    participant W as WhatsApp
    App->>A: POST sendText
    A-->>App: 202 queued (immediately)
    Note over A: random pause (1.5-4 s)
    A->>W: mark chat as read
    A->>W: "typing..."
    Note over A: typing time ~ message length (2-8 s)
    A->>W: "paused"
    A->>W: message
  1. Per-minute limit. Each session sends at most GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN messages per rolling minute (15 by default). Over the limit, the API answers 429.
  2. Human pause between GATEWAY_MIN_DELAY_MS and GATEWAY_MAX_DELAY_MS.
  3. Read, then type. The chat is marked as read and "typing..." is shown for a time proportional to the message (GATEWAY_MS_PER_CHAR), never shorter than GATEWAY_TYPING_DURATION_MS nor longer than GATEWAY_MAX_TYPING_MS, plus up to one second of jitter.
  4. One at a time per chat. A reply split in several messages arrives in order.
  5. Retries for transient errors (3 attempts with backoff). Permanent errors (number not on WhatsApp, forbidden) are not retried.

Audio messages show "recording audio..." instead of "typing...".

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text:
Variable Default GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN 15 Messages per minute per session. GATEWAY_MIN_DELAY_MS 1500 Shortest pause before typing. GATEWAY_MAX_DELAY_MS 4000 Longest pause before typing. GATEWAY_TYPING_DURATION_MS 2000 Shortest typing time. GATEWAY_MS_PER_CHAR 50 Typing time per character. GATEWAY_MAX_TYPING_MS 8000 Longest typing time.

Lower values send faster and look less human. The defaults are a safe starting point for customer service; raise them for cold outreach.

docs.title: Good practices
docs.text:
The best protection is behaviour, not code:

  • Warm up new numbers. Use a fresh number by hand for a few days before automating it, and grow the volume slowly.
  • Message people who expect it. Most bans start with users reporting spam.
  • Vary the text. Hundreds of identical messages are an easy signal.
  • Give a way out. "Reply STOP to stop receiving messages" and honour it.
  • Prefer replies over cold messages. Conversations started by the customer are far safer.

Warning

No tool can guarantee a number will not be banned. Arcanum reduces the risk; how you use it decides the rest.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Every running Arcanum serves its interactive documentation:

  • Swagger UI: http://<your-gateway>/docs. Click Authorize, paste your API key and use Try it out on any route.
  • OpenAPI 3.1 spec: http://<your-gateway>/docs/openapi.json, ready to import into Postman, Insomnia, Bruno or a client generator.

The spec is tested against the router on every build, so it always lists exactly the routes that exist.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors are JSON with an error field:

{"error": "invalid instance name \"../x\": use 1-64 letters, digits, '-' or '_'"}
Code When 400 Invalid body or field. 401 Missing or invalid API key. 404 Session not found. 409 Session name already exists. 413 Request larger than GATEWAY_MAX_BODY_MB. 429 Per-minute send limit reached. 501 Route planned but not implemented yet. 503 Session not connected.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Every route requires the API key, except GET /health and the documentation (/docs, /docs/openapi.json).

docs.title: Sending the key
docs.text:
Use either header:

X-Api-KeyBearerPythonNode.jsGo 
curl -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" http://localhost:3100/api/instance/fetchInstances

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCANUM_KEY" http://localhost:3100/api/instance/fetchInstances

import os, httpx

arcanum = httpx.Client(
    base_url="http://localhost:3100",
    headers={"X-Api-Key": os.environ["ARCANUM_KEY"]},
    timeout=30,
)
print(arcanum.get("/api/instance/fetchInstances").json())

const res = await fetch("http://localhost:3100/api/instance/fetchInstances", {
  headers: { "X-Api-Key": process.env.ARCANUM_KEY },
});
console.log(await res.json());

req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", "http://localhost:3100/api/instance/fetchInstances", nil)
req.Header.Set("X-Api-Key", os.Getenv("ARCANUM_KEY"))
resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

A missing or wrong key returns:

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="arcanum"

{"error":"missing or invalid API key (send X-Api-Key or Authorization: Bearer)"}

docs.title: Choosing a key
docs.text:
Set GATEWAY_API_KEY to a long random value. 32 random bytes is a good default:

openssl rand -hex 32
Situation What happens GATEWAY_API_KEY set That key is required. Keys shorter than 32 characters log a warning. Not set A random key is generated on every start and printed in the log. GATEWAY_AUTH_DISABLED=true No key at all. Only for your own machine: anyone who reaches the port controls your numbers.

The key is compared in constant time, so response timing does not leak it.

docs.title: Rotating the key
docs.text:
1. Generate a new key and update your application to send it.
  2. Restart Arcanum with the new GATEWAY_API_KEY. Sessions reconnect on their own; nobody needs to scan a QR code again.

Keep the key out of the browser

The key gives full control over every session. Call Arcanum from your backend, never from front-end code that users can inspect.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Arcanum is configured only through environment variables, all prefixed with GATEWAY_.

docs.title: Server and security
docs.text: Variable Default Description GATEWAY_PORT 3100 HTTP port. GATEWAY_API_KEY (generated) Key required on every route. Use 32+ random characters (openssl rand -hex 32). If empty, a temporary key is generated on each start and printed in the log. GATEWAY_AUTH_DISABLED false Turns authentication off. Local development only. GATEWAY_MAX_BODY_MB 64 Largest request accepted, in MB (base64 media counts here). GATEWAY_DB_PATH ./data (/data in Docker) Folder with one SQLite file (<name>.db) and one settings file (<name>.json) per session. Created with permission 700, files 600.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: Variable Default Description GATEWAY_DASHBOARD true Serves the web dashboard at /. false turns it off. GATEWAY_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD (empty) Dashboard sign-in password. Empty: sign in with the API key. Set it, long and random.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text: Variable Default Description GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORWARD_URL (empty) Default webhook URL for every session. {instance} is replaced by the session name. GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORMAT simple simple (flat JSON) or meta (WhatsApp Cloud API envelope). See Webhooks. GATEWAY_META_APP_SECRET (empty) Secret for the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC. Without it, deliveries are not signed.

docs.title: Anti-ban
docs.text: Variable Default Description GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN 15 Messages per minute per session. GATEWAY_MIN_DELAY_MS 1500 Shortest pause before typing. GATEWAY_MAX_DELAY_MS 4000 Longest pause before typing. GATEWAY_TYPING_DURATION_MS 2000 Shortest typing time. GATEWAY_MS_PER_CHAR 50 Typing time per character. GATEWAY_MAX_TYPING_MS 8000 Longest typing time.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Variable Default Description GATEWAY_LOG_FORMAT text text for people, json for log collectors (Loki, CloudWatch, Datadog...). GATEWAY_LOG_LEVEL info debug, info, warn or error.

Logs never contain message text, phone numbers or contact names at info level. At debug, the sender of each webhook delivery is logged to help troubleshooting.

docs.title: Example .env
docs.text:
.env
GATEWAY_API_KEY=3f9c...64-hex-characters...
GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORWARD_URL=https://your-app.example.com/webhooks/whatsapp/{instance}
GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORMAT=simple
GATEWAY_META_APP_SECRET=another-long-random-value
GATEWAY_LOG_FORMAT=json

Never commit .env

It holds the keys to every connected number. The repository .gitignore already excludes it.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: Arcanum ships a web dashboard inside the same binary. Open the gateway address in a browser (http://localhost:3100) and sign in.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
Setting Password to use GATEWAY_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD set That password. Recommended: you never paste the API key in a browser. Not set The API key (GATEWAY_API_KEY). GATEWAY_DASHBOARD=false The dashboard is turned off; / returns 404.

Sessions last 12 hours and end when the gateway restarts. After 10 wrong passwords from the same address in 15 minutes, sign-in is locked for that address.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text: Overview Connected sessions, sessions waiting for a QR code, messages received and sent, webhook deliveries and failures, uptime and version. Refreshes every few seconds. Sessions Create a session, show its QR code (it refreshes by itself until the phone scans it) or a pairing code, see status and number, restart, disconnect or delete. Deleting unlinks the device from the phone and removes the session files. Session page Webhook URL and on/off switch, Send test (a signed {"event":"test"} delivery with the HTTP status and time), the last 100 deliveries with status and duration, and per-session settings. Webhooks Every session's webhook at a glance. Export downloads a JSON file with all of them; Import applies such a file to the sessions that exist (handy when moving servers). Logs The gateway log, live, filterable by level, with pause. Message text, phone numbers and secrets (API key, passwords) never appear. Settings Light or dark theme, English or Portuguese, links to the API and this guide.

docs.title: How it is protected
docs.text:
• The session cookie is HttpOnly (scripts cannot read it), SameSite=Strict (other sites cannot use it) and Secure over HTTPS.
  • Every dashboard request also carries an anti-CSRF header; a cookie alone is refused.
  • The page only loads code from the gateway itself (strict Content Security Policy) and cannot be embedded in another site.
  • Sessions are kept in memory as hashes: nothing to steal from disk.

Use HTTPS

Over plain HTTP the password travels in clear text. On anything but localhost, put Arcanum behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS (Deployment).

docs.title: Developing the dashboard
docs.text:
The source is in web/ (React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS):

cd web
npm ci
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5180, proxies the API to a gateway on :3100
npm run build      # outputs to internal/dashboard/dist, embedded by `go build`

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: A production setup has three parts: Arcanum on a private port, a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front, and backups of the session files.

docs.title: Docker Compose with HTTPS (Caddy)
docs.text:
Caddy gets and renews the TLS certificate automatically.

compose.yaml
services:
  arcanum:
    image: ghcr.io/rafaeldourado9/arcanum:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${ARCANUM_KEY:?set ARCANUM_KEY}
      GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORWARD_URL: ${ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_URL}
      GATEWAY_META_APP_SECRET: ${ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET}
      GATEWAY_LOG_FORMAT: json
    volumes:
      - arcanum-data:/data
    # no "ports": only Caddy reaches it, through the internal network

  caddy:
    image: caddy:2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    command: caddy reverse-proxy --from wa.example.com --to arcanum:3100
    volumes:
      - caddy-data:/data

volumes:
  arcanum-data:
  caddy-data:
.env
ARCANUM_KEY=...                 # openssl rand -hex 32
ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_URL=https://your-app.example.com/webhooks/whatsapp/{instance}
ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=...      # openssl rand -hex 32

Point the DNS of wa.example.com to the server and run docker compose up -d.

Nginx instead of Caddy 
server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name wa.example.com;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/wa.example.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/wa.example.com/privkey.pem;

    client_max_body_size 64m;          # same as GATEWAY_MAX_BODY_MB

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3100;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_read_timeout 300s;
    }
}

docs.title: Sizing
docs.text: Each session uses roughly 20-50 MB of RAM. A 1 GB machine comfortably runs dozens of sessions. CPU use is negligible except when sending large media.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
Each <session>.db in the data volume is a logged-in WhatsApp session. Back the volume up, encrypted, and restore it to bring sessions back without scanning QR codes.

# stop for a consistent copy (a few seconds of downtime)
docker compose stop arcanum
docker run --rm -v arcanum-data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
  tar czf /backup/arcanum-$(date +%F).tgz -C /data .
docker compose start arcanum

Encrypt the archive (for example with age or gpg) before sending it off the server.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
docker compose pull arcanum
docker compose up -d arcanum

Sessions reconnect on their own after the restart. Arcanum shuts down gracefully on SIGTERM: it finishes in-flight requests and closes every session file cleanly. Update regularly: WhatsApp periodically stops accepting old client versions.

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text:
The image has a built-in HEALTHCHECK on /health. For Kubernetes or a load balancer:

livenessProbe:
  httpGet: { path: /health, port: 3100 }
  periodSeconds: 30

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: In five minutes you will have Arcanum running, a WhatsApp number connected and your first message sent.

docs.title: 1. Run Arcanum
docs.text:
DockerDocker ComposeFrom source 
export ARCANUM_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
echo "Your API key: $ARCANUM_KEY"

docker run -d --name arcanum -p 3100:3100 \
  -e GATEWAY_API_KEY="$ARCANUM_KEY" \
  -v arcanum-data:/data \
  ghcr.io/rafaeldourado9/arcanum:latest
compose.yaml
services:
  arcanum:
    image: ghcr.io/rafaeldourado9/arcanum:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:3100:3100"   # only this machine; use a reverse proxy for the internet
    environment:
      GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${ARCANUM_KEY:?set ARCANUM_KEY}
      GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORWARD_URL: https://your-app.example.com/webhooks/whatsapp/{instance}
      GATEWAY_META_APP_SECRET: ${ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET}
    volumes:
      - arcanum-data:/data

volumes:
  arcanum-data:

ARCANUM_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" docker compose up -d

Requires Go 1.26+ and a C compiler (the SQLite driver uses CGO).

git clone https://github.com/rafaeldourado9/arcanum.git
cd arcanum
go build -o arcanum ./cmd/gateway
GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" ./arcanum

Check that it is up (this route is public):

curl http://localhost:3100/health

{"instances":0,"sessions":{},"status":"ok","version":"v1.1.0"}

Prefer clicking?

Open http://localhost:3100 and sign in to the dashboard: it creates sessions, shows the QR code and configures webhooks. Add -e GATEWAY_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD=... to the command above to use a password instead of the API key. Other ways to install (script, systemd, Windows, Kubernetes) are in Installation.

Forgot the key?

If you start Arcanum without GATEWAY_API_KEY, it generates a temporary key and prints it in the log (docker logs arcanum). It changes on every restart, so set your own.

docs.title: 2. Create a session
docs.text:
A session (instance) is one WhatsApp number. Give it a name made of letters, digits, - or _.

curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/instance/create \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"instanceName": "sales"}'

docs.title: 3. Connect the number
docs.text:
QR codePairing code

Open the QR code as an image and scan it with WhatsApp > Linked devices > Link a device:

curl -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" \
  "http://localhost:3100/api/instance/connect/sales?format=png" -o qr.png

Without ?format=png the same route returns JSON with the QR code as a data URL, ready for an <img src> in your own UI.

No camera at hand? Ask for an 8-character code and type it in WhatsApp > Linked devices > Link with phone number instead:

curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/instance/pair/sales \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"phone": "5511999999999"}'

Then check the status until it says connected:

curl -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" \
  http://localhost:3100/api/instance/connectionState/sales

docs.title: 4. Send your first message
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/message/sendText/sales \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"number": "5511999999999", "text": "Hello from Arcanum!"}'

{"ok": true, "status": "queued"}

The answer comes right away (202 Accepted). The message goes out a few seconds later, after the typing indicator and a human-like pause: that is the anti-ban layer at work.

docs.title: 5. Receive messages
docs.text:
Point a webhook at your application and every incoming message arrives as a POST:

curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/events/webhook/sales \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://your-app.example.com/webhooks/whatsapp", "enabled": true}'

See Webhooks for the payload and how to verify the signature.

docs.title: What next
docs.text:
• Interactive API docs: every route, with a "Try it out" button.
  • Deployment: HTTPS, backups and updates.
  • Security: the checklist before going live.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Arcanum is a single static binary with the dashboard built in. Pick the way that fits your server; they all run the same thing.

Method Best for Docker Most setups. One command, easy updates. Install script A Linux or macOS machine without Docker. systemd service A Linux server, started on boot, hardened. Binary download Windows, or full manual control. Kubernetes Clusters. From source Contributors.

Whatever you choose, open http://<server>:3100 for the dashboard and /docs for the interactive API.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
docker run -d --name arcanum -p 3100:3100 \
  -e GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  -e GATEWAY_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD="choose-a-long-password" \
  -v arcanum-data:/data \
  ghcr.io/rafaeldourado9/arcanum:latest

The image is distroless (no shell, no package manager), runs as an unprivileged user, works with a read-only root filesystem and has a built-in health check. It is published for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, signed with Cosign and shipped with an SBOM.

Ready-made Compose files live in the repository's deploy/ folder:

This machine onlyPublic server with HTTPS 
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rafaeldourado9/arcanum/main/deploy/docker-compose.yml
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rafaeldourado9/arcanum/main/.env.example -o .env
# edit .env: set GATEWAY_API_KEY and GATEWAY_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD
docker compose up -d

curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rafaeldourado9/arcanum/main/deploy/docker-compose.caddy.yml
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rafaeldourado9/arcanum/main/.env.example -o .env
echo "ARCANUM_DOMAIN=wa.example.com" >> .env   # its DNS must point to this server
# edit .env: set GATEWAY_API_KEY and GATEWAY_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD
docker compose -f docker-compose.caddy.yml up -d

Caddy obtains and renews the Let's Encrypt certificate. Arcanum itself is not published on any port.

Verify the image signature 
cosign verify ghcr.io/rafaeldourado9/arcanum:latest \
  --certificate-identity-regexp 'https://github.com/rafaeldourado9/arcanum/' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com

docs.title: Install script (Linux, macOS)
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://arcanum.rafaeldourado.tech/install.sh | sh

The script detects your OS and CPU, downloads the latest release, checks its SHA-256 against checksums.txt and installs /usr/local/bin/arcanum. Then:

GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" GATEWAY_DB_PATH="$HOME/.arcanum" arcanum

Options: --version v1.1.0 pins a version; ARCANUM_BIN_DIR=$HOME/.local/bin installs without sudo. Prefer to read it first? It is short.

docs.title: systemd service
docs.text:
On a Linux server, let the script set everything up:

curl -fsSL https://arcanum.rafaeldourado.tech/install.sh | sh -s -- --systemd

It creates:

  • the system user arcanum and /var/lib/arcanum (permission 700) for the sessions;
  • /etc/arcanum/arcanum.env, readable only by root, with a random API key and dashboard password (sudo grep -E 'API_KEY|PASSWORD' /etc/arcanum/arcanum.env shows them);
  • the arcanum service, enabled on boot.

The unit is heavily sandboxed (no new privileges, read-only system, private /tmp, no capabilities, restricted system calls). Day to day:

sudo systemctl status arcanum
sudo journalctl -u arcanum -f
sudo systemctl restart arcanum   # after editing /etc/arcanum/arcanum.env

docs.title: Binary download
docs.text:
Every release has archives for Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64, plus checksums.txt and a build provenance attestation.

Windows (PowerShell)Linux / macOS 
# after extracting arcanum_<version>_windows_amd64.zip

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
kubectl create namespace arcanum
kubectl -n arcanum create secret generic arcanum \
  --from-literal=GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  --from-literal=GATEWAY_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -hex 12)"

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
Requires Go 1.26+ and Node.js 22+ (for the dashboard). No C compiler needed.

git clone https://github.com/rafaeldourado9/arcanum.git && cd arcanum
(cd web && npm ci && npm run build)        # builds the dashboard into the binary
go build -o arcanum ./cmd/gateway
GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" ./arcanum

Skip the dashboard step and the binary still works: / explains how to build it.

docs.title: Upgrading from 1.0
docs.text:
Version 1.1 runs as a non-root user (UID 65532). A data volume created by 1.0 belongs to root, so give it to the new user once:

docker run --rm -v arcanum-data:/data alpine chown -R 65532:65532 /data

Version 1.1 also requires the API key on every route: set GATEWAY_API_KEY and send it from your application (Authentication).

docs.title: Sending messages
docs.text: All send routes take the session name in the path and a JSON body. number accepts a phone number with country code (5511999999999, punctuation is ignored) or a full JID received in a webhook (5511999999999@s.whatsapp.net, 123456789@lid).

docs.title: Common answers
docs.text: Code Meaning 200 Sent. Body has messageId. 202 Text queued (see below). 400 Missing or invalid field. 404 Session does not exist. 429 Per-minute limit reached: {"error":"rate limit exceeded","current":15,"limit":15}. 503 Session is not connected: {"error":"not connected","status":"qr"}.

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/message/sendText/sales \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"number": "5511999999999", "text": "Your order has shipped."}'

{"ok": true, "status": "queued"}

Text is queued: the answer is immediate and the anti-ban layer sends it a few seconds later (typing indicator, human pause). Messages to the same chat go out in the order you sent them. If a message still fails after 3 attempts, your webhook receives a send_failed event.

PythonNode.jsGo 
arcanum.post("/api/message/sendText/sales",
             json={"number": "5511999999999", "text": "Your order has shipped."})

await fetch("http://localhost:3100/api/message/sendText/sales", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "X-Api-Key": process.env.ARCANUM_KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ number: "5511999999999", text: "Your order has shipped." }),
});

body := strings.NewReader(`{"number":"5511999999999","text":"Your order has shipped."}`)
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", base+"/api/message/sendText/sales", body)
req.Header.Set("X-Api-Key", key)
req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

docs.title: Media
docs.text:
Image, audio, video or document. media is the file content in base64; Arcanum does not download URLs (that keeps it from being used to fetch internal addresses).

curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/message/sendMedia/sales \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{
        \"number\": \"5511999999999\",
        \"mediatype\": \"document\",
        \"mimetype\": \"application/pdf\",
        \"fileName\": \"invoice-1042.pdf\",
        \"caption\": \"Your invoice\",
        \"media\": \"$(base64 -w0 invoice-1042.pdf)\"
      }"
Field Notes mediatype image, audio, video or document (default). mimetype e.g. image/jpeg, audio/ogg, video/mp4, application/pdf. caption Shown under images, videos and documents. fileName Name shown for documents.

Audio shows "recording audio..." before it is sent. Requests are limited to GATEWAY_MAX_BODY_MB (64 MB by default), which includes the base64 overhead (~33%).

PythonNode.js 
import base64, pathlib

data = base64.b64encode(pathlib.Path("invoice-1042.pdf").read_bytes()).decode()
arcanum.post("/api/message/sendMedia/sales", json={
    "number": "5511999999999", "mediatype": "document",
    "mimetype": "application/pdf", "fileName": "invoice-1042.pdf", "media": data,
})

import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const media = (await readFile("invoice-1042.pdf")).toString("base64");
await fetch(`${base}/api/message/sendMedia/sales`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "X-Api-Key": key, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ number: "5511999999999", mediatype: "document",
    mimetype: "application/pdf", fileName: "invoice-1042.pdf", media }),
});

docs.title: Other chat actions
docs.text:
Route Body Does POST /api/chat/markMessageAsRead/{name} {"readMessages":[{"remoteJid":"...","id":"..."}]} Blue ticks. POST /api/chat/checkWhatsAppNumbers/{name} {"numbers":["5511..."]} Which numbers have WhatsApp. POST /api/chat/updateProfileName/{name} {"name":"Acme Support"} Display name. POST /api/chat/updateProfileStatus/{name} {"status":"Replies in minutes"} "About" text. POST /api/chat/updateProfilePicture/{name} {"picture":"<base64 jpeg>"} Profile photo. POST /api/instance/setPresence/{name} {"presence":"available"} Online / offline.

Planned

archiveChat (returns 501) and findChats, findContacts, findMessages (return empty lists) need a message store and are on the roadmap.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
GET /health is public and safe to expose to a load balancer: it shows counts only, never session names or numbers.

{
  "status": "ok",
  "version": "v1.1.0",
  "instances": 3,
  "sessions": {"connected": 2, "qr": 1}
}

Alert when a session you expect to be connected stays in another state.

docs.title: Prometheus metrics
docs.text:
GET /metrics (requires the API key) returns counters in the Prometheus text format:

Metric Type Meaning arcanum_sessions{status} gauge Sessions by status. arcanum_messages_received_total counter Incoming messages forwarded to the webhook. arcanum_messages_sent_total counter Messages sent through the API. arcanum_messages_send_errors_total counter Sends that failed after retries. arcanum_webhook_delivered_total counter Webhook deliveries answered with 2xx. arcanum_webhook_failed_total counter Webhook deliveries that failed. arcanum_http_requests_total{code} counter API responses by HTTP status. prometheus.yml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: arcanum
    metrics_path: /metrics
    authorization:
      credentials: <your GATEWAY_API_KEY>
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["arcanum:3100"]

docs.title: Useful alerts
docs.text:
groups:
  - name: arcanum
    rules:
      - alert: ArcanumSessionDown
        expr: arcanum_sessions{status="connected"} < 1
        for: 5m
      - alert: ArcanumWebhookFailing
        expr: rate(arcanum_webhook_failed_total[5m]) > 0
        for: 10m
      - alert: ArcanumUnauthorizedRequests
        expr: rate(arcanum_http_requests_total{code="401"}[5m]) > 1
        for: 5m

A steady flow of 401 usually means someone is probing the API, or a client is using an old key.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Set GATEWAY_LOG_FORMAT=json to ship logs to Loki, CloudWatch, Datadog or any collector:

{"time":"2026-11-23T18:28:16Z","level":"INFO","msg":"arcanum gateway listening","addr":":3100","version":"v1.1.0","auth":true}

Use GATEWAY_LOG_LEVEL=debug temporarily to troubleshoot webhook deliveries.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Arcanum controls real WhatsApp accounts. Whoever reaches the API, or copies a session file, can read and send messages as that number. Treat it like a database.

docs.title: Checklist before going live
docs.text:
• [x] GATEWAY_API_KEY set to 32+ random characters.
  • [x] GATEWAY_AUTH_DISABLED not set.
  • [x] GATEWAY_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD set (or GATEWAY_DASHBOARD=false if you do not use the dashboard).
  • [x] Port 3100 not open to the internet: only a reverse proxy with HTTPS reaches it.
  • [x] GATEWAY_META_APP_SECRET set, and your webhook verifies X-Hub-Signature-256.
  • [x] Data volume backed up encrypted, with restricted access.
  • [x] The API key lives in your backend only, never in front-end code.
  • [x] Updates applied regularly (new releases fix security issues and keep up with WhatsApp).

docs.title: What Arcanum does for you
docs.text: Area Protection Authentication API key on every route except /health, /docs and the dashboard sign-in; constant-time comparison; random key generated when none is set, so it is never open by accident. Input Session names restricted to A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ (they become file names: no path traversal). Request size limit and HTTP timeouts. Webhooks (SSRF) Only http/https; cloud metadata and link-local addresses refused, checked again at connection time (DNS rebinding); redirects not followed; no credentials in the URL. Media Base64 only: Arcanum never downloads URLs on your behalf. Privacy Message text, phone numbers and contact names are not logged at info level. HTTP headers nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, strict Content-Security-Policy, Cache-Control: no-store, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer. Dashboard Separate password, HttpOnly + SameSite=Strict session cookie, anti-CSRF header on every request, sign-in lockout after 10 failures, strict CSP, sessions stored as hashes in memory. See Dashboard. Container Distroless image (no shell, no package manager), unprivileged user (UID 65532), works with a read-only root filesystem and no capabilities; reproducible build with go mod verify; signed with Cosign, with SBOM and provenance. Files Session files and settings created with permission 600, data folder 700. systemd The provided unit runs sandboxed: no new privileges, read-only system, private /tmp, no capabilities, filtered system calls. Shutdown Graceful on SIGTERM: session files closed cleanly. Supply chain Every change runs the race detector, go vet, staticcheck, govulncheck, gosec and a Trivy image scan. Dependabot updates dependencies weekly.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text: Please do not open a public issue. Use Security > Report a vulnerability on the GitHub repository. You get an answer within 72 hours. Details in SECURITY.md.

docs.title: Privacy and compliance
docs.text: Messages pass through Arcanum in memory on their way to your webhook; Arcanum does not keep a message history. Session files hold encryption keys and contact identifiers. If you serve people in Brazil (LGPD) or Europe (GDPR), you are the data controller: document the purpose, secure the server and the webhook endpoint, and honour opt-out requests.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text: A session (or instance) is one WhatsApp number connected to Arcanum. You can run as many as your machine handles; each has its own webhook, settings and rate limit.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> disconnected: create
    disconnected --> qr: connect (new number)
    disconnected --> connecting: connect (already paired)
    qr --> connected: QR scanned / code typed
    connecting --> connected
    connected --> connecting: network drop (auto-reconnect)
    connected --> disconnected: logout
    disconnected --> [*]: delete
Status Meaning disconnected Not connected. Call connect. qr Waiting for the QR code to be scanned (or the pairing code to be typed). connecting Opening the connection or reconnecting after a drop. connected Ready to send and receive.

Paired sessions are stored on disk (GATEWAY_DB_PATH: <name>.db for the WhatsApp session, <name>.json for its webhook and settings) and reconnect automatically when Arcanum restarts, with the same configuration. Network drops are retried forever with a backoff of up to 30 seconds.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/instance/create \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "instanceName": "sales",
        "webhook": "https://your-app.example.com/webhooks/whatsapp/sales"
      }'
Field Required Notes instanceName yes 1-64 characters: A-Z a-z 0-9 - _. It becomes a file name, so nothing else is accepted. webhook no Webhook URL for this session. Without it, GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORWARD_URL is used. webhookEvents no Defaults to ["messages", "status"].

Answers 201 with the session, 409 if the name exists, 400 if the name or the webhook URL is invalid.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
QR code (JSON)QR code (PNG)Pairing code 
curl -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" http://localhost:3100/api/instance/connect/sales

{
  "instanceName": "sales",
  "status": "qr",
  "qr": "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo..."
}

The qr field drops straight into an HTML image: <img src="{qr}">.

curl -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" \
  "http://localhost:3100/api/instance/connect/sales?format=png" -o qr.png

curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/instance/pair/sales \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"phone": "5511999999999"}'

Type the returned code in WhatsApp: Linked devices > Link a device > Link with phone number instead.

The QR code rotates every ~20 seconds; poll connectionState (or qr) to show the latest one. Calling connect again while waiting returns the current QR code: it never opens a second connection.

docs.title: Inspect
docs.text:
# One session
curl -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" http://localhost:3100/api/instance/connectionState/sales

# All sessions, with settings and webhook configuration
curl -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" http://localhost:3100/api/instance/fetchInstances

docs.title: Restart, disconnect, delete
docs.text:
Action Route Effect Restart POST /api/instance/restart/{name} Reconnects. Nothing to scan. Disconnect DELETE /api/instance/logout/{name} Drops the connection; the session stays paired. Delete DELETE /api/instance/delete/{name} Unlinks the device from the phone, closes the session and removes its files. It does not come back after a restart.

Unlinking from the phone

If you remove the device in WhatsApp > Linked devices, the session becomes invalid and needs a new QR code. Delete it in Arcanum and create it again.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/settings/sales \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"groupsIgnore": true}'
Setting Status Effect groupsIgnore available Group messages are not forwarded to the webhook. rejectCalls planned Stored, no effect yet. alwaysOnline planned Stored, no effect yet. readMessages planned Stored, no effect yet. readStatus planned Stored, no effect yet. syncFullHistory planned Stored, no effect yet.

Group, status (stories), broadcast and channel messages are never forwarded today: Arcanum focuses on one-to-one conversations.

docs.title: The QR code does not appear
docs.text:
1. Check the logs: docker logs arcanum. Look for lines starting with [whatsmeow].
  2. A line like QR event "err-client-outdated" means WhatsApp no longer accepts this version of the client library. Update Arcanum (docker compose pull && docker compose up -d).
  3. Make sure the session exists (fetchInstances) and call connect again; the QR code rotates every ~20 seconds.

docs.title: 401 missing or invalid API key
docs.text: The key is missing or different from GATEWAY_API_KEY. If you never set one, Arcanum generated a temporary key at startup: find it in the log, then set your own.

docs.title: 503 not connected
docs.text: The session is not connected. Check connectionState. If it is qr, scan the code. If it keeps going back to connecting, check the server's internet connection.

docs.title: 429 rate limit exceeded
docs.text: The session reached GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN. Wait and retry, or spread the sends. See Anti-ban before raising the limit.

docs.title: Messages arrive late
docs.text: That is the anti-ban layer: a pause, then "typing..." for a time that grows with the message length. Expected total: roughly 4-13 seconds per message with the defaults.

docs.title: My webhook receives nothing
docs.text:
• Is the webhook enabled? GET /api/events/webhook/{name}.
  • Is the URL reachable from the Arcanum container? localhost inside a container is the container itself: use the service name (http://api:8000) or the host address.
  • Does your endpoint answer 2xx within 30 seconds? Check arcanum_webhook_failed_total and the logs with GATEWAY_LOG_LEVEL=debug.
  • Group, status and broadcast messages are not forwarded.

docs.title: The reply goes to a strange number ending in @lid
docs.text: WhatsApp sometimes hides the phone number behind an internal ID (@lid). Arcanum resolves it to the phone number when it can. When it cannot, reply to the from value exactly as you received it: the message still arrives.

docs.title: Sessions disappeared after a restart
docs.text: The data volume was not persisted. Mount /data as a named volume or a host folder (-v arcanum-data:/data), and never delete it: it holds the logged-in sessions.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text: Open an issue on GitHub with the Arcanum version (/health), what you did, what you expected, and the relevant log lines. Remove API keys and phone numbers before posting.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text: Arcanum posts every incoming WhatsApp message to your application as JSON. You choose the URL, the format and a secret to sign each delivery.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
One URL for every session (env)Per session (API) 
GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORWARD_URL=https://your-app.example.com/webhooks/whatsapp/{instance}
GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORMAT=simple        # or "meta"
GATEWAY_META_APP_SECRET=change-me    # HMAC secret (strongly recommended)

{instance} is replaced by the session name, so your app knows which number the message arrived on (/webhooks/whatsapp/sales).

curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/events/webhook/sales \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://your-app.example.com/webhooks/whatsapp/sales", "enabled": true}'

GET on the same route returns the current configuration. "enabled": false pauses deliveries without losing the URL.

The URL must be http or https. Cloud metadata and link-local addresses (169.254.169.254, ...) are refused, checked again at connection time, and redirects are not followed. Private networks are allowed, so a webhook to another container (http://api:8000/...) works.

The configuration of each session is saved to disk and survives restarts. The dashboard shows it, edits it and exports it.

docs.title: Test and history
docs.text:
# send a signed {"event":"test","instance":"sales","timestamp":"..."} and get the result
curl -X POST -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" http://localhost:3100/api/events/webhook/sales/test

{"time":"2026-11-23T19:13:03Z","event":"test","status":200,"ok":true,"durationMs":84}

GET /api/events/webhook/{name}/deliveries lists the last 100 deliveries (event, HTTP status, duration, error). Bodies are not stored, so no personal data is kept.

docs.title: Export and import
docs.text:
curl -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" http://localhost:3100/api/events/webhooks/export -o webhooks.json
# on the new server, after creating the sessions:
curl -X POST -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @webhooks.json http://localhost:3100/api/events/webhooks/import

Import only updates sessions that exist; unknown names and invalid URLs are reported as skipped with the reason.

docs.title: Payload: simple format (default)
docs.text:
Flat and easy to read. Example of a text message:

{
  "from": "5511999999999@s.whatsapp.net",
  "from_me": false,
  "push_name": "Maria",
  "type": "text",
  "text": "Hi, is my order on the way?",
  "message_id": "3EB0C431C26A1916E2F5",
  "timestamp": "1764000000"
}
Field Notes from The contact of the conversation as a JID. Always the phone number (@s.whatsapp.net) when WhatsApp lets Arcanum resolve it; @lid otherwise. Reply to this value as-is. from_me true when the message was sent by the connected number itself, including messages a human types on the phone. Always present. push_name Contact's display name, when available. type text, image, audio, video, document, sticker, location or unknown. text Message text, or the caption of a media message. message_id Use it for reactions and read receipts. timestamp Unix seconds, as a string. media Present for media: mimetype, data (base64), filename, caption. location Present for location: latitude, longitude, name, address. Media and location examples image
{
  "from": "5511999999999@s.whatsapp.net", "from_me": false, "type": "image",
  "text": "the broken part", "message_id": "3EB0...", "timestamp": "1764000000",
  "media": {"mimetype": "image/jpeg", "data": "/9j/4AAQSk...", "filename": "", "caption": "the broken part"}
}
location
{
  "from": "5511999999999@s.whatsapp.net", "from_me": false, "type": "location",
  "message_id": "3EB0...", "timestamp": "1764000000",
  "location": {"latitude": -23.5614, "longitude": -46.6559, "name": "Head office"}
}

docs.title: Payload: meta format
docs.text:
Same envelope as the WhatsApp Cloud API (Meta), so code written for the official API can read Arcanum messages with the same parser. Set GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORMAT=meta.

{
  "object": "whatsapp_business_account",
  "entry": [{
    "id": "gateway",
    "changes": [{
      "field": "messages",
      "value": {
        "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
        "metadata": {"display_phone_number": "gateway", "phone_number_id": "gateway"},
        "contacts": [{"wa_id": "5511999999999@s.whatsapp.net", "profile": {"name": "Maria"}}],
        "messages": [{
          "from": "5511999999999@s.whatsapp.net",
          "from_me": false,
          "id": "3EB0C431C26A1916E2F5",
          "timestamp": "1764000000",
          "type": "text",
          "text": {"body": "Hi, is my order on the way?"}
        }]
      }
    }]
  }]
}

docs.title: Other events
docs.text: These are flat in both formats and carry an event field:

docs.title: Typing
docs.text:
Sent while the contact is typing, so your bot can wait before answering.

{"event": "typing", "from": "5511999999999@s.whatsapp.net", "state": "composing"}

state is composing or paused.

docs.title: Send failures
docs.text:
A queued text that still failed after 3 attempts:

{"event": "send_failed", "to": "5511999999999", "text": "Your order has shipped."}

docs.title: Human takeover with from_me
docs.text:
When someone answers a customer from the phone, Arcanum forwards that message with from_me: true and from set to the customer. Use it to pause your bot in that conversation:

if payload["from_me"]:
    pause_bot(conversation=payload["from"], minutes=30)
    return

docs.title: Verify the signature
docs.text:
With GATEWAY_META_APP_SECRET set, every delivery has:

X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body>

Compute the HMAC over the raw bytes you received (before parsing JSON) and compare in constant time. Reject the request if it does not match.

Python (FastAPI)Node.js (Express)GoPHP 
import hashlib, hmac, os
from fastapi import FastAPI, Header, HTTPException, Request

SECRET = os.environ["ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET"].encode()
app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/webhooks/whatsapp/{instance}")
async def whatsapp(instance: str, request: Request,
                   x_hub_signature_256: str = Header(default="")):
    body = await request.body()
    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(SECRET, body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, x_hub_signature_256):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="bad signature")

    payload = await request.json()
    if payload.get("event") == "typing":
        return {"ok": True}
    if payload.get("from_me"):
        return {"ok": True}          # a human answered from the phone

    enqueue_reply(instance, payload)  # do the slow work in a queue
    return {"ok": True}

import crypto from "node:crypto";
import express from "express";

const SECRET = process.env.ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET;
const app = express();

// raw body: the signature is over the exact bytes Arcanum sent
app.post("/webhooks/whatsapp/:instance", express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), (req, res) => {
  const expected = "sha256=" + crypto.createHmac("sha256", SECRET).update(req.body).digest("hex");
  const got = req.get("X-Hub-Signature-256") || "";
  const ok = got.length === expected.length &&
    crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(got), Buffer.from(expected));
  if (!ok) return res.status(401).send("bad signature");

  const payload = JSON.parse(req.body);
  if (!payload.event && !payload.from_me) queueReply(req.params.instance, payload);
  res.json({ ok: true });
});

app.listen(8000);

func whatsapp(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(r.Body, 70<<20))
    if err != nil {
        http.Error(w, "read error", http.StatusBadRequest)
        return
    }
    mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(os.Getenv("ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET")))
    mac.Write(body)
    expected := "sha256=" + hex.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
    if !hmac.Equal([]byte(expected), []byte(r.Header.Get("X-Hub-Signature-256"))) {
        http.Error(w, "bad signature", http.StatusUnauthorized)
        return
    }

    var msg struct {
        Event  string `json:"event"`
        From   string `json:"from"`
        FromMe bool   `json:"from_me"`
        Type   string `json:"type"`
        Text   string `json:"text"`
    }
    _ = json.Unmarshal(body, &msg)
    if msg.Event == "" && !msg.FromMe {
        go handleMessage(r.PathValue("instance"), msg)
    }
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
}

$body = file_get_contents('php://input');
$expected = 'sha256=' . hash_hmac('sha256', $body, getenv('ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET'));
if (!hash_equals($expected, $_SERVER['HTTP_X_HUB_SIGNATURE_256'] ?? '')) {
    http_response_code(401);
    exit('bad signature');
}
$payload = json_decode($body, true);
// ...

docs.title: Delivery behaviour
docs.text:
• Each event is posted once, with a 30-second timeout. Any 2xx answer counts as delivered; anything else is logged and counted in arcanum_webhook_failed_total (metrics).
  • Answer fast. Return 200 right away and do the work (AI calls, database writes) in a background queue. A slow endpoint delays nothing else in Arcanum, but a timeout means the event is not retried.
  • Messages older than 10 minutes (the backlog WhatsApp delivers after a long time offline or right after pairing) are not forwarded, so your bot does not answer old conversations.
  • The events list is stored with the configuration; today every event is delivered. Per-event filtering and automatic retries are on the roadmap.

docs.title: Test locally
docs.text:
Expose your local app with a tunnel and point the webhook to it:

# terminal 1: your app on :8000
# terminal 2:
cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000   # or: ngrok http 8000

Then set the printed HTTPS URL as the webhook and send a message to the connected number.

docs.title: Início
docs.text:
docker run -d --name arcanum -p 3100:3100 \
  -e GATEWAY_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  -v arcanum-data:/data \
  ghcr.io/rafaeldourado9/arcanum:latest

  • Leve e rápido

    Um binário Go sobre a whatsmeow. Poucas dezenas de MB de memória por sessão, sobe em milissegundos, roda até num Raspberry Pi.

  • Anti-ban nativo

    "Digitando..." proporcional ao tamanho da mensagem, pausa aleatória humana, limite por minuto e uma mensagem por vez em cada conversa. Ligado por padrão em todo envio.

  • Vários números, uma API

    Crie quantas sessões precisar. Cada uma tem seu webhook, suas configurações e seu limite. As sessões sobrevivem a reinícios.

  • Webhooks confiáveis

    Assinatura HMAC-SHA256 em toda entrega, formato compatível com a Cloud API da Meta ou um formato simples, e o campo fromMe para seu bot saber quando um humano assumiu.

  • Seguro por padrão

    Chave de API em toda rota, validação de entrada, proteção contra SSRF nos webhooks, nada de dado pessoal no log, container sem root e varredura de vulnerabilidades no CI.

  • Open source, MIT

    Leia cada linha, faça fork, rode onde quiser. Sem chave de licença, sem telemetria.

docs.title: API de WhatsApp que você mesmo hospeda
docs.text:
O Arcanum é um gateway de WhatsApp open source escrito em Go. Um único binário pequeno conecta seus números de WhatsApp e entrega uma API REST, webhooks assinados e uma camada anti-ban que se comporta como uma pessoa digitando. Sem navegador, sem Node, sem ficar preso a fornecedor.

Comece em 5 minutos GitHub

docs.title: Como se encaixa
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Sua aplicação] -- REST + chave de API --> B[Arcanum]
    B -- protocolo do WhatsApp Web --> C[(WhatsApp)]
    C -- mensagens recebidas --> B
    B -- webhook assinado --> A

Sua aplicação chama o Arcanum para enviar mensagens. O Arcanum mantém as sessões do WhatsApp conectadas e envia cada mensagem recebida para o seu webhook.

docs.title: Próximos passos
docs.text:
• Primeiros passos: rode, leia o QR code e envie a primeira mensagem.
  • Webhooks: receba mensagens e confira a assinatura.
  • Produção: coloque no ar com HTTPS.

Não é uma API oficial

O Arcanum fala com o WhatsApp pelo mesmo protocolo do WhatsApp Web. Não tem vínculo com o WhatsApp nem com a Meta. Mensagens automáticas podem levar ao banimento do número: respeite os termos do WhatsApp, fale só com quem espera seu contato e mantenha a camada anti-ban ligada.

docs.title: Anti-ban
docs.text: O WhatsApp fica de olho em contas que agem como máquina: resposta instantânea, rajadas de mensagens iguais, nada de "digitando...". O Arcanum faz cada envio de texto parecer escrito por uma pessoa.

docs.title: O que acontece em cada texto
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Sua aplicação
    participant A as Arcanum
    participant W as WhatsApp
    App->>A: POST sendText
    A-->>App: 202 queued (na hora)
    Note over A: pausa aleatória (1,5-4 s)
    A->>W: marca a conversa como lida
    A->>W: "digitando..."
    Note over A: tempo de digitação ~ tamanho da mensagem (2-8 s)
    A->>W: "pausado"
    A->>W: mensagem
  1. Limite por minuto. Cada sessão envia no máximo GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN mensagens por minuto, em janela móvel (15 por padrão). Acima disso, a API responde 429.
  2. Pausa humana entre GATEWAY_MIN_DELAY_MS e GATEWAY_MAX_DELAY_MS.
  3. Lê, depois digita. A conversa é marcada como lida e o "digitando..." aparece por um tempo proporcional à mensagem (GATEWAY_MS_PER_CHAR), nunca menor que GATEWAY_TYPING_DURATION_MS nem maior que GATEWAY_MAX_TYPING_MS, mais até um segundo de variação.
  4. Uma por vez em cada conversa. Uma resposta dividida em várias mensagens chega na ordem.
  5. Novas tentativas em erros passageiros (3 tentativas, com espera crescente). Erros permanentes (número sem WhatsApp, proibido) não são repetidos.

Áudios mostram "gravando áudio..." no lugar de "digitando...".

docs.title: Ajustes
docs.text:
Variável Padrão GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN 15 Mensagens por minuto por sessão. GATEWAY_MIN_DELAY_MS 1500 Menor pausa antes de digitar. GATEWAY_MAX_DELAY_MS 4000 Maior pausa antes de digitar. GATEWAY_TYPING_DURATION_MS 2000 Menor tempo digitando. GATEWAY_MS_PER_CHAR 50 Tempo digitando por caractere. GATEWAY_MAX_TYPING_MS 8000 Maior tempo digitando.

Valores menores enviam mais rápido e parecem menos humanos. Os padrões são um ponto de partida seguro para atendimento; aumente para prospecção fria.

docs.title: Boas práticas
docs.text:
A melhor proteção é o comportamento, não o código:

  • Aqueça números novos. Use o número na mão por alguns dias antes de automatizar e aumente o volume aos poucos.
  • Fale com quem espera. A maioria dos banimentos começa com usuários denunciando spam.
  • Varie o texto. Centenas de mensagens idênticas são um sinal fácil.
  • Dê uma saída. "Responda SAIR para não receber mais mensagens", e respeite.
  • Prefira responder a puxar conversa. Conversas iniciadas pelo cliente são muito mais seguras.

Warning

Nenhuma ferramenta garante que um número não será banido. O Arcanum reduz o risco; o jeito de usar decide o resto.

docs.title: Referência da API
docs.text:
Todo Arcanum em execução serve a própria documentação interativa:

  • Swagger UI: http://<seu-gateway>/docs. Clique em Authorize, cole sua chave de API e use Try it out em qualquer rota.
  • Especificação OpenAPI 3.1: http://<seu-gateway>/docs/openapi.json, pronta para importar no Postman, Insomnia, Bruno ou num gerador de cliente.

A especificação é testada contra o roteador a cada build, então lista sempre exatamente as rotas que existem.

docs.title: Erros
docs.text:
Os erros são JSON com o campo error:

{"error": "invalid instance name \"../x\": use 1-64 letters, digits, '-' or '_'"}
Código Quando 400 Corpo ou campo inválido. 401 Chave de API faltando ou inválida. 404 Sessão não encontrada. 409 Já existe sessão com esse nome. 413 Pedido maior que GATEWAY_MAX_BODY_MB. 429 Limite de envios por minuto atingido. 501 Rota planejada, ainda não implementada. 503 Sessão não conectada.

docs.title: Autenticação
docs.text: Toda rota exige a chave de API, menos GET /health e a documentação (/docs e /docs/openapi.json).

docs.title: Enviando a chave
docs.text:
Use qualquer um destes cabeçalhos:

X-Api-KeyBearerPythonNode.jsGo 
curl -H "X-Api-Key: $ARCANUM_KEY" http://localhost:3100/api/instance/fetchInstances

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCANUM_KEY" http://localhost:3100/api/instance/fetchInstances

import os, httpx

arcanum = httpx.Client(
    base_url="http://localhost:3100",
    headers={"X-Api-Key": os.environ["ARCANUM_KEY"]},
    timeout=30,
)
print(arcanum.get("/api/instance/fetchInstances").json())

const res = await fetch("http://localhost:3100/api/instance/fetchInstances", {
  headers: { "X-Api-Key": process.env.ARCANUM_KEY },
});
console.log(await res.json());

req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", "http://localhost:3100/api/instance/fetchInstances", nil)
req.Header.Set("X-Api-Key", os.Getenv("ARCANUM_KEY"))
resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

Sem chave, ou com a chave errada, a resposta é:

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="arcanum"

{"error":"missing or invalid API key (send X-Api-Key or Authorization: Bearer)"}

docs.title: Escolhendo a chave
docs.text:
Defina GATEWAY_API_KEY com um valor longo e aleatório. 32 bytes aleatórios é um bom padrão:

openssl rand -hex 32
Situação O que acontece GATEWAY_API_KEY definida Essa chave é exigida. Chave com menos de 32 caracteres gera um aviso no log. Não definida Uma chave aleatória é gerada a cada início e mostrada no log. GATEWAY_AUTH_DISABLED=true Nenhuma chave. Só na sua própria máquina: quem alcançar a porta controla seus números.

A chave é comparada em tempo constante, então o tempo de resposta não a revela.

docs.title: Trocando a chave
docs.text:
1. Gere uma chave nova e atualize sua aplicação para enviá-la.
  2. Reinicie o Arcanum com a nova GATEWAY_API_KEY. As sessões reconectam sozinhas; ninguém precisa ler QR code de novo.

Mantenha a chave longe do navegador

A chave dá controle total sobre todas as sessões. Chame o Arcanum pelo seu backend, nunca por código de front-end que o usuário consegue inspecionar.

docs.title: Configuração
docs.text: O Arcanum é configurado só por variáveis de ambiente, todas com o prefixo GATEWAY_.

docs.title: Servidor e segurança
docs.text: Variável Padrão Descrição GATEWAY_PORT 3100 Porta HTTP. GATEWAY_API_KEY (gerada) Chave exigida em toda rota. Use 32+ caracteres aleatórios (openssl rand -hex 32). Vazia: uma chave temporária é gerada a cada início e mostrada no log. GATEWAY_AUTH_DISABLED false Desliga a autenticação. Só para desenvolvimento local. GATEWAY_MAX_BODY_MB 64 Maior pedido aceito, em MB (mídia em base64 conta aqui). GATEWAY_DB_PATH ./data (/data no Docker) Pasta com um arquivo SQLite (<nome>.db) e um de configuração (<nome>.json) por sessão. Criada com permissão 700, arquivos 600.

docs.title: Painel
docs.text: Variável Padrão Descrição GATEWAY_DASHBOARD true Serve o painel web em /. false desliga. GATEWAY_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD (vazia) Senha do login do painel. Vazia: o login usa a chave de API. Defina, longa e aleatória.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text: Variável Padrão Descrição GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORWARD_URL (vazia) URL de webhook padrão para todas as sessões. {instance} é trocado pelo nome da sessão. GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORMAT simple simple (JSON plano) ou meta (envelope da Cloud API do WhatsApp). Veja Webhooks. GATEWAY_META_APP_SECRET (vazia) Segredo do HMAC em X-Hub-Signature-256. Sem ele, as entregas não são assinadas.

docs.title: Anti-ban
docs.text: Variável Padrão Descrição GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN 15 Mensagens por minuto por sessão. GATEWAY_MIN_DELAY_MS 1500 Menor pausa antes de digitar. GATEWAY_MAX_DELAY_MS 4000 Maior pausa antes de digitar. GATEWAY_TYPING_DURATION_MS 2000 Menor tempo digitando. GATEWAY_MS_PER_CHAR 50 Tempo digitando por caractere. GATEWAY_MAX_TYPING_MS 8000 Maior tempo digitando.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Variável Padrão Descrição GATEWAY_LOG_FORMAT text text para pessoas, json para coletores de log (Loki, CloudWatch, Datadog...). GATEWAY_LOG_LEVEL info debug, info, warn ou error.

No nível info, os logs nunca trazem texto de mensagem, telefone ou nome de contato. Em debug, o remetente de cada entrega de webhook aparece, para ajudar a investigar problemas.

docs.title: Exemplo de .env
docs.text:
.env
GATEWAY_API_KEY=3f9c...64-caracteres-hex...
GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORWARD_URL=https://seu-app.exemplo.com/webhooks/whatsapp/{instance}
GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORMAT=simple
GATEWAY_META_APP_SECRET=outro-valor-longo-e-aleatorio
GATEWAY_LOG_FORMAT=json

Nunca suba o .env para o Git

Ele guarda as chaves de todos os números conectados. O .gitignore do repositório já o exclui.

docs.title: Painel
docs.text: O Arcanum traz um painel web dentro do mesmo binário. Abra o endereço do gateway no navegador (http://localhost:3100) e entre.

docs.title: Entrando
docs.text:
Configuração Senha para usar GATEWAY_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD definida Essa senha. Recomendado: você nunca cola a chave de API no navegador. Não definida A chave de API (GATEWAY_API_KEY). GATEWAY_DASHBOARD=false O painel fica desligado; a / responde 404.

A sessão dura 12 horas e termina quando o gateway reinicia. Depois de 10 senhas erradas do mesmo endereço em 15 minutos, o login fica bloqueado para esse endereço.

docs.title: O que dá para fazer
docs.text: Visão geral Sessões conectadas, sessões esperando QR code, mensagens recebidas e enviadas, entregas e falhas de webhook, tempo no ar e versão. Atualiza a cada poucos segundos. Sessões Criar uma sessão, mostrar o QR code (ele se atualiza sozinho até o celular ler) ou um código de pareamento, ver status e número, reiniciar, desconectar ou apagar. Apagar desconecta o aparelho do celular e remove os arquivos da sessão. Página da sessão URL do webhook e chave liga/desliga, Enviar teste (uma entrega assinada {"event":"test"} com o status HTTP e o tempo), as últimas 100 entregas com status e duração, e as configurações da sessão. Webhooks O webhook de todas as sessões numa olhada. Exportar baixa um JSON com todos; Importar aplica esse arquivo às sessões que existem (útil ao trocar de servidor). Logs O log do gateway ao vivo, com filtro por nível e pausa. Texto de mensagem, telefones e segredos (chave de API, senhas) nunca aparecem. Configurações Tema claro ou escuro, inglês ou português, links para a API e para este guia.

docs.title: Como ele é protegido
docs.text:
• O cookie da sessão é HttpOnly (scripts não leem), SameSite=Strict (outros sites não usam) e Secure no HTTPS.
  • Todo pedido do painel também leva um cabeçalho anti-CSRF; só o cookie é recusado.
  • A página só carrega código do próprio gateway (Content Security Policy restrita) e não pode ser embutida em outro site.
  • As sessões ficam em memória, guardadas por hash: nada para roubar do disco.

Use HTTPS

Em HTTP puro a senha trafega sem criptografia. Fora do localhost, coloque o Arcanum atrás de um proxy reverso com HTTPS (Produção).

docs.title: Desenvolvendo o painel
docs.text:
O código fica em web/ (React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS):

cd web
npm ci
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5180, repassa a API para um gateway na :3100
npm run build      # gera internal/dashboard/dist, embutido pelo `go build`

docs.title: Produção
docs.text: Uma instalação de produção tem três partes: o Arcanum numa porta privada, um proxy reverso com HTTPS na frente e backup dos arquivos de sessão.

docs.title: Docker Compose com HTTPS (Caddy)
docs.text:
O Caddy emite e renova o certificado TLS sozinho.

compose.yaml
services:
  arcanum:
    image: ghcr.io/rafaeldourado9/arcanum:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${ARCANUM_KEY:?defina ARCANUM_KEY}
      GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_FORWARD_URL: ${ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_URL}
      GATEWAY_META_APP_SECRET: ${ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET}
      GATEWAY_LOG_FORMAT: json
    volumes:
      - arcanum-data:/data
    # sem "ports": só o Caddy alcança, pela rede interna

  caddy:
    image: caddy:2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    command: caddy reverse-proxy --from wa.exemplo.com --to arcanum:3100
    volumes:
      - caddy-data:/data

volumes:
  arcanum-data:
  caddy-data:
.env
ARCANUM_KEY=...                 # openssl rand -hex 32
ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_URL=https://seu-app.exemplo.com/webhooks/whatsapp/{instance}
ARCANUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=...      # openssl rand -hex 32

Aponte o DNS de wa.exemplo.com para o servidor e rode docker compose up -d.

Nginx no lugar do Caddy 
server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name wa.exemplo.com;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/wa.exemplo.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/wa.exemplo.com/privkey.pem;

    client_max_body_size 64m;          # igual a GATEWAY_MAX_BODY_MB

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3100;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_read_timeout 300s;
    }
}

docs.title: Dimensionamento
docs.text: Cada sessão usa por volta de 20 a 50 MB de memória. Uma máquina de 1 GB roda dezenas de sessões com folga. O uso de CPU é mínimo, exceto no envio de mídias grandes.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
Cada <sessão>.db no volume de dados é uma sessão de WhatsApp logada. Faça backup do volume, criptografado, e restaure para trazer as sessões de volta sem ler QR code.

# para por alguns segundos, para a cópia sair consistente
docker compose stop arcanum
docker run --rm -v arcanum-data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
  tar czf /backup/arcanum-$(date +%F).tgz -C /data .
docker compose start arcanum

Criptografe o arquivo (por exemplo com age ou gpg) antes de tirá-lo do servidor.

docs.title: Atualizar
docs.text:
docker compose pull arcanum
docker compose up -d arcanum

As sessões reconectam sozinhas depois do reinício. O Arcanum desliga de forma limpa no SIGTERM: termina os pedidos em andamento e fecha cada arquivo de sessão direito. Atualize com frequência: de tempos em tempos o WhatsApp deixa de aceitar versões antigas do cliente.

docs.title: Checagem de saúde
docs.text:
A imagem já tem um HEALTHCHECK em /health. Para Kubernetes ou um balanceador:

livenessProbe:
  httpGet: { path: /health, port: 3100 }
  periodSeconds: 30

docs.title: Primeiros passos
docs.text: Em cinco minutos você terá o Arcanum rodando, um número de WhatsApp conectado e a primeira mensagem enviada.

docs.title: 1. Rode o Arcanum
docs.text:
DockerDocker ComposePelo código-fonte
